title: The host control process writes a root probe that TermAl reports as a read-only child's change
outcome: A read-only TermAl child session is never reported as having changed a project file only because its host `engram control` process resolved the project root identity.
acceptance: A test covers whichever side owns the fix

An `engram control` process started with an explicit --project-file resolves its root identity without writing a marker file into the project root, or TermAl excludes that marker from a read-only child's changed files

completion.summary: The host probe no longer writes into the project root. probe_host_path_policy(project_file) looks the project file up again under its name with every ASCII letter's case inverted. A miss means case-sensitive. A hit is decided by the root listing: one entry answering to the name, ignoring ASCII case, means it folds; two or more mean case-sensitive. Each spelling is re-checked for change, and identities are never compared across spellings. When the probe cannot decide, the identity stays unresolved (the WARNING, and the host supplies --host-path-policy), with no marker fallback. A create-denied or read-only checkout now resolves. Unit tests script every decision and race. The root-probe harness calibrates its watcher, runs a real `engram control`, doctor, readiness, the agent words and MCP with no root write of any name, and keeps a real-binary WARNING control. Five review rounds; the last was clean from both reviewers. Landed as 0a7aba8 (pushed) and installed as build 96ac5fe3d0a4; both stores reported ready with the policy matched. TermAl was told. Independent evaluation passed both criteria.
